exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Concern for the Elephants
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: I'm really concerned about the African elephants these days.
Ben: Why is that? What's happening to them?
Anna: They're being hunted for their tusks, and their habitat is getting smaller.
Ben: That's terrible. Can elephants move to another place?
Anna: It's hard. They need very large living spaces, so they can't adapt easily.
Ben: So what is being done to help them?
Anna: The authorities are building special parks and asking people not to buy elephant products.
Ben: I see. When the buying stops, the killing can stop too.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 担心非洲象;它们因象牙被捕猎、栖息地变小;大象需要很大的生存空间,难以适应;为帮助它们,当局在修建专门的园区,并劝人们不要购买大象制品;只有停止购买,捕杀才会停止。

questions.stem: Why is Anna worried about the African elephants?
options: They are being hunted and their habitat is shrinking.
They are too many in number.
They have moved to the city.

questions.stem: Why is it hard for elephants to move elsewhere?
options: They need very large living spaces.
They prefer to stay in zoos.

questions.stem: What are the authorities doing to help?
options: Building special parks and asking people not to buy elephant products.

questions.stem: What does Ben say at the end of the talk?
options: When the buying stops, the killing can stop too.

questions.stem: How would you describe Anna's feeling about the elephants?
options: She is angry at the elephants.
She is concerned and wants to help.
She thinks they are safe already.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 An Alarming Rate
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Our planet's wildlife is dying out at an alarming rate.
Between one hundred and fifty and two hundred species become extinct every day.
This mass extinction is caused by hunting, habitat loss and pollution.
We must make people aware of the problem before it is too late.
Each of us can help to save the endangered wildlife.
exercises.translation_cn: 地球上的野生动物正以惊人的速度消失;每天有150到200个物种灭绝;这场大规模灭绝由捕猎、栖息地丧失和污染造成;我们必须趁还不太晚让人们意识到这个问题;我们每个人都能帮助拯救濒危野生动物。

questions.stem: At what rate is the planet's wildlife dying out?
How many species become extinct every day?
What causes this mass extinction?
What must we do before it is too late?
options: Make people aware of the problem.

questions.stem: According to the passage, who can help save wildlife?

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 A Weekend of Birdwatching
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lily: We got up so early this morning to search for wild birds!
Tom: Yes, the best time to watch birds is just after sunrise.
Lily: I brought a field guide so we can look up the birds we see.
Tom: Good idea. And my dad lent me these binoculars, so we can see them better.
Lily: Our club does more than watch, though. We also clean up the habitats.
Tom: That's right. We build bird feeders and put paper cut-outs on the windows.
Lily: The cut-outs stop birds from crashing into the glass.
Tom: Exactly. Little actions like these really help to protect the birds.
exercises.translation_cn: Lily 和 Tom 一早起来去找野鸟;日出后是观鸟最佳时间;Lily 带了图鉴查鸟名,Tom 带了望远镜看得更清;他们的俱乐部不只观鸟,还清理栖息地;搭鸟食台、在窗上贴纸样,防止鸟撞玻璃;这些小行动真的能帮助保护鸟类。

questions.stem: Why did Lily and Tom get up so early?
What did Lily bring with her?
options: A field guide to look up the birds.

questions.stem: What are the binoculars used for?
Why does the club put paper cut-outs on windows?
options: To stop birds from crashing into the glass.

questions.stem: What does the club do besides watching birds?
options: It cleans habitats and builds feeders.
It sells the birds at a market.
It keeps the birds in cages.

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 The Tibetan Antelope's Comeback
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In the 1980s and 1990s, the Tibetan antelope was in great danger.
Hunters were shooting the animals to make profits from their fur.
To save the species, the government placed it under national protection.
Volunteers watched over the herds day and night to keep them safe.
Thanks to these measures, the antelope was later removed from the endangered list.
exercises.translation_cn: 上世纪八九十年代,藏羚羊处境危险;猎人射杀它们,靠其毛皮牟利;为拯救该物种,政府把它置于国家保护之下;志愿者日夜看护羊群以保护它们;多亏这些措施,藏羚羊后来被移出了濒危名单。

questions.stem: When was the Tibetan antelope in great danger?
Why were hunters shooting the antelopes?
options: To make profits from their fur.
To move them to a reserve.

questions.stem: What did the government do to save the species?
options: It opened the area to hunters.
It placed the antelope under national protection.

questions.stem: How did the volunteers help?
options: They watched over the herds day and night.
They left the area at night.

questions.stem: What finally happened to the Tibetan antelope?
options: It was removed from the endangered list.
It was sold at a market.

exercises.title: U2 听力·对话 Designing a Poster
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: We need to make a poster about an endangered animal. Where do we start?
Jack: First, let's write a title that is simple, interesting and a little unusual.
Mia: Good. Then we should choose one powerful image to catch people's eyes.
Jack: Right. A strong picture can stir up emotions much faster than words.
Mia: After that, we write the name of the species and why it is in danger.
Jack: And we must tell readers exactly what we want them to think and do.
Mia: So our poster should clearly call for action, like 'Don't buy animal products.'
Jack: Perfect. Then everyone who sees it will know how to help.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 和 Jack 要做一张濒危动物海报;先写一个简洁、有趣、略不寻常的标题;再选一张有冲击力的图片抓住眼球;强烈的画面比文字更能激起情感;然后写明物种名称和濒危原因;还要明确告诉读者希望他们想什么、做什么;海报应清楚地呼吁行动,比如'不要购买动物制品';这样看到的人就知道如何帮忙了。

questions.stem: What should the poster's title be like?
options: Simple, interesting and a little unusual.

questions.stem: Why do they want one powerful image?
options: To stir up emotions faster than words.

questions.stem: What information should the poster include about the animal?
options: The species name and why it is in danger.
The name of the designer only.

questions.stem: What must the poster clearly tell readers?
options: What they want readers to think and do.

questions.stem: What action does their poster call for?

exercises.title: U2 听力·短文 Baby Elephants in Kenya
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: At a centre in Kenya, keepers look after baby elephants that have lost their mothers.
The young elephants are fed milk from bottles every few hours.
The keepers also sing to them and play with them so they do not feel alone.
The most important thing each baby must learn is how to live in the wild again.
So far, the centre has helped hundreds of orphan elephants return to nature.
exercises.translation_cn: 在肯尼亚的一个中心,饲养员照料失去母亲的小象;每隔几小时用奶瓶喂奶;饲养员还给它们唱歌、陪它们玩,让它们不孤单;每只小象最重要的是学会重新在野外生活;到目前为止,中心已帮助数百只孤儿大象回归自然。

questions.stem: Which baby elephants does the centre look after?
options: Those that are already grown up.
Those that live in the city.
Those that have lost their mothers.

questions.stem: How are the baby elephants fed?
options: With milk from bottles every few hours.

questions.stem: Why do the keepers sing and play with them?
options: So that the elephants do not feel alone.

questions.stem: What is the most important thing each baby must learn?
options: How to live in the wild again.

questions.stem: How many orphan elephants has the centre helped so far?
